q: The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 applies to employees drawing wages up to ___ per month.
Under the Act, a wage period must not exceed ___.
In establishments employing fewer than 1,000 persons, wages must be paid before the ___ day of the following month.
In establishments employing 1,000 or more persons, wages must be paid before the ___ day of the following month.
Under the Act, wages must be paid in ___.

options.B: current coin, currency notes, cheque or bank credit

q: Which of the following is excluded from wages under the Act?

options.B: bonus not forming part of the terms of employment

q: The employer contribution to the provident fund is ___.
Deductions from wages may be made only if they are ___.
In any wage period, a fine imposed on an employee must not exceed ___ of his wages.
No fine can be imposed on an employed person who is below ___ years of age.
Before imposing a fine, the employer must ___.

options.A: give the person an opportunity to show cause

q: Sums realised as fines must be applied to ___.
Deduction for absence from duty must be ___.

options.A: equal to a full day wage per hour
options.C: proportionate to the period of absence

q: Deduction for damage to or loss of goods must not exceed ___.

options.D: the actual amount of the damage or loss

q: Before making a deduction for damage or loss, the employer must ___.

options.C: give the employee an opportunity to show cause

q: Deductions for house accommodation supplied by the employer are ___.
Deductions for amenities and services supplied by the employer are ___.
Where advances are being recovered, total deductions from wages must not exceed ___.
Where no advance is being recovered, total deductions must not exceed ___.
Deduction of income-tax payable by the employed person is ___.
Deductions for payments to co-operative societies require ___.

options.B: the written authorisation of the employee

q: Claims arising under the Act are decided by ___.

options.A: the Authority appointed under the Act

q: An application to the Authority must ordinarily be presented within ___.
An appeal against the Authority order lies to ___.

options.B: the Court of Small Causes or District Court

q: The appeal must be filed within ___ of the Authority order.
The Act applies to persons employed in ___.

options.B: factories, railways and other industrial establishments

q: The term employed person under the Act excludes persons employed in a ___ capacity.
Under the Act, wages must be paid ___.
Deduction towards a loan advanced for house-building is ___.
An Inspector under the Act may ___.
Every employer must maintain ___.

options.B: registers of wages, fines and deductions

q: The notice specifying acts and omissions for which fines may be imposed must be ___.
Every fine imposed must be recorded in ___.
For piece-rated workers, deduction for absence is based on ___.

options.B: the earnings for the period of absence

q: Wages under the Act includes ___.
Travelling allowance paid to an employed person is ___.
The appropriate Government may extend the Act to ___.
Deduction of life insurance premium is allowed with ___.

options.C: the written authorisation of the employee

q: The maximum wage period permitted under the Act is ___.
On termination of employment, wages must be paid before the expiry of ___.
Deductions for contributions to the Prime Minister National Relief Fund require ___.
An employer who fails to pay wages by the due date is liable to ___.
The 2017 amendment raised the wage ceiling from ₹18,000 to ___.
Payment of wages by cheque or bank account credit was enabled by the amendment of ___.
Deduction for trade union subscription is allowed only with ___.
A person aggrieved by an unauthorised deduction may apply to ___.
The Authority may direct refund of the deducted amount along with compensation up to ___.
For railway purposes, industrial establishment under the Act includes ___.
Railway servants drawing wages up to ___ per month are covered by the Act.
Which deduction is NOT authorised by the Act?
The register of fines must show ___.

options.A: the act or omission and the amount

q: Deductions from a railway servant wages for loss of railway property are governed by ___.

options.D: the damage-or-loss provisions of the Act

q: The wage ceiling of ₹24,000 refers to wages ___.
Wages means remuneration payable under ___.

options.A: the terms of employment, express or implied

q: Contravention of the Act deduction provisions attracts ___.
Inspectors appointed under the Act are deemed to be ___.
The State Government may appoint ___ for the purposes of the Act.
Payment of wages in kind is ___.
Deduction for house rent is permissible only when ___.
The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 was enacted to ___.

options.C: regulate wage payment and prevent unauthorised deductions
